rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Gameplay 3 Variants 3.1 Setup 3.2 Bruno's Variant 3.3 Tournament Mode Objective The objective is to make a full grid of 16 number tiles, winning the round. The numbers in each row must increase from left to right, and the numbers in each column must increase from top to bottom. You cannot have the same number twice in a row or column. Gameplay Shuffle 1 set of 1-20 for each player as a pot. Each player starts with 4 distinct numbers in a diagonal line. At the beginning of each of your turns, you may either draw a random tile from the pot or take a tile from the table (if there are any). You may play the tile you have as long as it is higher than each tile before it in the same row and column, and lower than each tile after it in the same row and column. If you take a tile from the table, you must play it. To play a tile, you may either play it in an empty space or replace an existing tile on your grid. If you replace a tile on your grid, or choose to discard a drawn tile, that tile goes onto the table. Example of a completed grid: Variants Setup Easy Setup: The first four tiles are automatically placed in ascending order from least in the top left to greatest in the bottom right. Michael's Setup: The first four tiles are drawn one at a time and placed one by one on the diagonal according to the player's choice. Bruno's Variant If you place a tile diagonally adjacent to a tile with the same number, you immediately get another turn. You can take several turns in a row in this way. Tournament Mode The game is played multiple times with each player getting a chance to go first. The winner of each round earns two points. The other players lose one point for each empty space on their grid. Highest total score And remember... have fun!

[Rating: 1/10] A slightly better version of rolling a dice with your friend then see who gets the bigger number

[Rating: 1/10] So incredibly bad, if you get a bad hand in the beginning, you're screwed, and if you and the person before you are going for the same numbers, you're screwed

[Rating: 1/10] The name fits the game perfectly. Straight from the start get lucky with your numbers or lose. Decision space is so narrow that it doesn't feel like you have a choice and player interaction is non-existent. At least its a quick game.

[Rating: 1.5/10] Not a game.  Pros: The graphic design is quite nice.   I'm only giving this a 1 because I don't consider it a game and am following the ratings guideline. It's a perfectly cromulent way to spend time.   Cons: There's no decisions, you just draw tiles and slot them in wherever they fit.   The game even removes agency, by not letting you place an illegal tile to either fix layer or to deny other players.   The random seeding in the beginning will likely decide the game, if you get a good spread you're already several turns ahead of the players that didn't. Why then bother playing it out?

[Rating: 2/10] Casual game as casual gets. Very random as often you wait for just one lucky number to win game, who gets it wins... maybe good for kids, I dont know... It sux for me.
